title: The secret life of red foxes
content: Red foxes are highly adaptable animals found across forests, grasslands, and even cities. They hunt small mammals at dusk and dawn, using their keen hearing to locate prey under snow.

title: Gray wolves and pack hunting
content: Gray wolves live and hunt in coordinated packs, using complex vocal and body-language signals to bring down large prey like elk and moose.

title: Why dogs became man's best friend
content: Domestic dogs descended from wolves tens of thousands of years ago and have since become loyal companions, working animals, and family pets around the world.

title: Black bears in North American forests
content: Black bears are opportunistic omnivores, foraging for berries, insects, and fish while preparing for winter hibernation.

title: The grace of white-tailed deer
content: White-tailed deer are common across North America, recognizable by the flash of their tail as they flee from predators through the underbrush.

title: Vulpes vulpes: the most widespread canid
content: Vulpes vulpes, known commonly as the red fox, has the widest geographic range of any member of the order Carnivora, spanning most of the Northern Hemisphere.
